newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says winter grain sowings up 3.6 percent.
newsitem.headline: France says winter grain sowings up 3.6 percent.

text.p: France's farm ministry, in its first estimate of sowings for next year's harvest, said on Thursday the country's total winter grain area had risen 3.6 percent from last year to 6.634 million hectares.
Winter soft wheat sowings were up 3.5 percent at 4.909 million hectares and winter barley was up 4.9 percent at 1.132 million hectares, it said in a provisional forecast.
Most sowings except durum had been virtually completed when the ministry made its survey on December 1, statistics office SCEES said in a statement.
Winter durum, which was 79 percent sown, was 1.1 percent up from the previous year at 265,000 hectares.
Hybrid triticale, the next biggest winter crop, came in one percent higher at 203,000 hectares.
Oats were up 2.3 percent at 79,000 hectares and rye fell 0.9 percent to 47,000 hectares.
Overall winter grain sowings were 6.6 percent higher than the five-year average between 1991 and 1995.
